football_evidence.question: Can Iowa contain Northwestern’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Iowa, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 3.1 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Northwestern has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Northwestern’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.2% of its dropbacks, and Iowa’s defense sacks the quarterback on 12.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Iowa has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Iowa’s offense has allowed a sack on 2.9% of its dropbacks, and Northwestern’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
In his last two games (Michigan State and Rutgers), Chiles averaged 8.4 yards per attempt, against 10.3 in his five games before that.
In his last two games (Washington and Minnesota), Hecklinski averaged 7.7 yards per attempt, against 5.9 in his three games before that.
contradicting: When Northwestern has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Northwestern’s offense averages 9.3 yards per pass attempt, and Iowa’s defense allows 7.1 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When Northwestern has the ball (big plays through the air): Northwestern’s offense turns 13.9% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Iowa’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.7% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Iowa has the ball (big plays through the air): Iowa’s offense turns 8.8% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Northwestern’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

Aidan Chiles has completed 117 of 167 passes (70.1%) for 1,617 yards, 9.7 yards per attempt, 12 touchdowns and 1 interception in seven games for Northwestern, and has been sacked on 15 of 182 dropbacks.
quarterbacks: Aidan Chiles has completed 117 of 167 passes (70.1%) for 1,617 yards, 9.7 yards per attempt, 12 touchdowns and 1 interception in seven games for Northwestern, and has been sacked on 15 of 182 dropbacks.
